newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds fall in dull trade, yield gap narrows.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds fall in dull trade, yield gap narrows.

text.p: Danish bond prices fell back in lethargic trade in a dull market on Monday, with the 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowing nonetheless, but dealers expected little activity until after FOMC.
"We don't see anything of note happening on the bond market until tomorrow's FOMC meeting is over," one dealer lamented.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.22 point from Friday's close at 105.86, yielding 7.11 percent in turnover of only one billion crowns while its December future remained untraded at 105.18. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.02 point to 83.58.
The crown strengthened further in the wake of the weekend's Europe Ecofin meeting in Ireland, trading at 3.8419 per mark at 1000 gmt, up from around 3.8430 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 94 during the course of the morning.
